subject: maths
title: Year 6 Area of Rectangles
seo_title: Year 6 Area of Rectangles Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Establish the formula for the area of a rectangle and use it to solve practical problems
meta_desc: Free Year 6 area of rectangles worksheets for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6M02): length × width from grids, cm² and m² with decimals, missing sides, composite shapes and practical problems with tiles, turf and paint. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
key_sub: Put both sides in the same unit first. Width = area ÷ length. Split composite shapes into rectangles. Area is in cm² or m².
body_html:
Why area = length × width

Area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape. It is measured in square units: cm² (square centimetres) or m² (square metres).

Squares in a rectangle sit in equal rows. Count the squares in one row and the number of rows, then multiply.

Area of a rectangle = length × width. For a square, side × side.

Decimals and units

The formula works with decimals too. Both sides must be in the same unit before you multiply.

Example: mixed units

A rug is 2 m long and 50 cm wide. What is its area in m²?

Change 50 cm to 0.5 m. 2 × 0.5 = 1.

Answer: 1 m²

Finding a missing side

If you know the area and one side, divide: width = area ÷ length.

Example

A rectangle has an area of 15 m². It is 6 m long. How wide is it?

15 ÷ 6 = 2.5. Check: 6 × 2.5 = 15.

Answer: 2.5 m

Composite shapes

Split the shape into rectangles. Find each area, then add. Or take the big rectangle and subtract the missing part.

Practical problems

Example: turf

A backyard is 8 m by 6.5 m. Turf costs $12 per m². What does it cost?

Area: 8 × 6.5 = 52 m². Cost: 52 × $12 = $624.

Answer: $624

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Finding the perimeter (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26)Area = length × width: 8 × 5 = 40 cm²
Adding the length and width (8 + 5 = 13)Multiply, do not add
Mixing units (2 m × 50 cm = 100)Change to one unit first: 2 × 0.5 = 1 m²
Writing a remainder as a decimal (15 ÷ 6 = 2.3)15 ÷ 6 = 2.5, because 3 out of 6 is 0.5
Using the whole rectangle for an L-shapeSplit it, or subtract the missing corner
Writing m for an areaArea is in cm² or m². Length is in cm or m

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about area in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: They establish the formula for the area of a rectangle, length × width, and use it to solve practical problems (AC9M6M02). This includes decimals, cm² and m², missing sides and shapes made of rectangles.

faq.q: How do you explain area = length × width to a child?
faq.a: Cover the rectangle with 1 cm squares. The squares form equal rows, so the number of rows times the squares in each row gives the area, which is the width times the length.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a rectangle with decimals?
faq.a: Multiply the length by the width as usual, keeping both in the same unit. For example, 2.5 m × 4 m = 10 m².

faq.q: How does this help with Year 7 maths and NAPLAN?
faq.a: Year 7 students sit NAPLAN numeracy, which includes area problems. Being confident with length × width, missing sides and composite shapes in Year 6 prepares students for high school maths.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 2 rows of 7 squares: 2 × 7 = 14 cm². (18 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: A square has sides of 12 m. What is its area?
items.e: Length and width of a square are the same: 12 × 12 = 144 m².

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 6 squares in each row and 5 rows. 5 × 6 = 30 squares, so the area is 30 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 4 rows of 6 squares: 4 × 6 = 24 cm². (20 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 12 × 4 = 48 m². (32 m is the perimeter.)

items.q: Rectangle A is 6 cm by 4 cm. Rectangle B is 8 cm by 3 cm. Which has the larger area?
items.e: A: 6 × 4 = 24 cm². B: 8 × 3 = 24 cm². The areas are the same, even though the shapes are different (their perimeters are 20 cm and 22 cm).

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 7 squares in each row and 3 rows. 3 × 7 = 21 squares, so the area is 21 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: Which is the formula for the area of a rectangle?
items.e: Area counts the squares inside: rows × squares in each row, which is length × width. 2 × (length + width) gives the perimeter.

items.q: A rectangle is 15 m long and 6 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 15 × 6 = 90 m². (42 m is the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 4 rows of 9 squares: 4 × 9 = 36 cm². (26 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 3 rows of 5 squares: 3 × 5 = 15 cm². (16 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded square?
items.e: 5 rows of 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². (20 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 3 rows of 8 squares: 3 × 8 = 24 cm². (22 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is covered by 6 rows of 1 m² squares. There are 9 squares in each row. What is its area?
items.e: 6 rows of 9 squares: 6 × 9 = 54 squares, so the area is 54 m². Area is in square units (m²), not m.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². (26 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is 11 cm long and 8 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 11 × 8 = 88 cm². (38 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 9 × 7 = 63 cm². (32 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?
items.e: Length and width of a square are the same: 7 × 7 = 49 cm².

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 9 squares in each row and 4 rows. 4 × 9 = 36 squares, so the area is 36 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: A rectangle is 20 m long and 9 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 20 × 9 = 180 m². (58 m is the perimeter.)

sets.title: Area in cm² and m², with decimals

items.q: A rectangle is 2.5 m long and 1.6 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 2.5 × 1.6 = 4 m².

items.q: A rug is 2 m long and 50 cm wide. What is its area in square metres?
items.e: Use the same unit first: 50 cm = 0.5 m. Area = 2 × 0.5 = 1 m². 2 × 50 = 100 mixes metres and centimetres.

items.q: A rectangle is 5 m long and 1.2 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 5 × 1.2 = 6 m². Tip: 1 × 5 = 5 and 0.2 × 5 = 1, so 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 2.5 × 4 = 10 m². Tip: 2 × 4 = 8 and 0.5 × 4 = 2, so 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 1.5 × 6 = 9 m². Tip: 1 × 6 = 6 and 0.5 × 6 = 3, so 6 + 3 = 9.

items.q: A garden bed is 3 m long and 40 cm wide. What is its area in square metres?
items.e: 40 cm = 0.4 m. Area = 3 × 0.4 = 1.2 m². (120 comes from 3 × 40, which mixes units.)

items.q: A square has sides of 1.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: Square: side × side = 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25 m².

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
A rectangle is 8 m long and 0.5 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 8 × 0.5 = 4 m².

items.q: A rectangle is 6.5 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 6.5 × 4 = 26 cm². Tip: 6 × 4 = 24 and 0.5 × 4 = 2, so 24 + 2 = 26.

items.q: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3.5 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 8 × 3.5 = 28 cm². Tip: 3 × 8 = 24 and 0.5 × 8 = 4, so 24 + 4 = 28.

items.q: How many square centimetres are in 1 square metre?
items.e: 1 m² is a square 100 cm by 100 cm. 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm². 100 cm² is only one row of it.

items.q: A rectangle is 3 m long and 0.8 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 3 × 0.8 = 2.4 m².

items.q: A rectangle is 7.5 cm long and 2 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 7.5 × 2 = 15 cm². Tip: 7 × 2 = 14 and 0.5 × 2 = 1, so 14 + 1 = 15.

items.q: A poster is 1 m long and 60 cm wide. What is its area in square centimetres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Area = 100 × 60 = 6000 cm². (320 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 3.5 × 2 = 7 m². Tip: 3 × 2 = 6 and 0.5 × 2 = 1, so 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Which unit is best for the area of a postage stamp?
items.e: A stamp is only a few centimetres long and wide, so square centimetres (cm²) fit.

items.q: A rectangle is 12 cm long and 0.5 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 12 × 0.5 = 6 cm².

items.q: Which unit is best for the area of a school basketball court?
items.e: A court is tens of metres long and wide, so square metres (m²) fit. m measures length, not area.

items.q: A square has sides of 2.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: Square: side × side = 2.5 × 2.5 = 6.25 m².

sets.title: Find the missing side from the area

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 240 m². One side is 16 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 240 ÷ 16 = 15 m. Check: 16 × 15 = 240 m².

items.q: A square has an area of 49 cm². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 49. 7 × 7 = 49, so each side is 7 cm. (49 ÷ 4 would be the side if 49 were the perimeter.)

items.q: A square has an area of 144 cm². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 144. 12 × 12 = 144, so each side is 12 cm. (144 ÷ 4 would be the side if 144 were the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 96 cm². One side is 8 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 cm. Check: 8 × 12 = 96 cm².

items.q: A rectangular rug has an area of 18 m². One side is 4 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Other side = 18 ÷ 4 = 4.5 m. The remainder 2 is 2 out of 4, which is 0.5, so the answer is 4.5 m, not 4.2 m. Check: 4 × 4.5 = 18 m².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 150 cm². One side is 10 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 150 ÷ 10 = 15 cm. Check: 10 × 15 = 150 cm².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 108 m². One side is 9 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 108 ÷ 9 = 12 m. Check: 9 × 12 = 108 m².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 63 m². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 63 ÷ 9 = 7 m. Check: 9 × 7 = 63 m².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 40 cm² and a length of 8 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: First find the width: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 cm. Then perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 90 m². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 90 ÷ 15 = 6 m. Check: 15 × 6 = 90 m².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 48 cm². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm. Check: 8 × 6 = 48 cm².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 54 cm² and a length of 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: First find the width: 54 ÷ 9 = 6 cm. Then perimeter = 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 cm.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 210 cm². One side is 14 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 210 ÷ 14 = 15 cm. Check: 14 × 15 = 210 cm².

items.q: A rectangular rug has an area of 15 m². One side is 6 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Other side = 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5 m. The remainder 3 is 3 out of 6, which is 0.5, so the answer is 2.5 m, not 2.3 m. Check: 6 × 2.5 = 15 m².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 84 cm². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 84 ÷ 12 = 7 cm. Check: 12 × 7 = 84 cm².

items.q: A rectangular rug has an area of 22 m². One side is 4 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Other side = 22 ÷ 4 = 5.5 m. The remainder 2 is 2 out of 4, which is 0.5, so the answer is 5.5 m, not 5.2 m. Check: 4 × 5.5 = 22 m².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 56 cm². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 cm. Check: 7 × 8 = 56 cm².

items.q: A square has an area of 81 m². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 81. 9 × 9 = 81, so each side is 9 m. (81 ÷ 4 would be the side if 81 were the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 132 m². One side is 11 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 132 ÷ 11 = 12 m. Check: 11 × 12 = 132 m².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 72 m². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so the missing side = area ÷ known side: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 m. Check: 6 × 12 = 72 m².

items.q: A shape is made of two rectangles that do not overlap: 4 m by 3.5 m and 2 m by 1.5 m. What is its total area?
items.e: 4 × 3.5 = 14 m² and 2 × 1.5 = 3 m². Total: 14 + 3 = 17 m². Multiplying the added sides, (4 + 2) × (3.5 + 1.5) = 30, does not work.

items.q: A rectangle is cut out of a larger rectangle. What is the area of the shaded part?
items.e: Big rectangle: 20 × 12 = 240. Hole: 10 × 4 = 40. Shaded part: 240 − 40 = 200 m².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 9 × 5 = 45 and 20 × 7 = 140. Add them: 45 + 140 = 185 m². (Or 20 × 12 − 11 × 5 = 185 m².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 5 = 40 and 18 × 7 = 126. Add them: 40 + 126 = 166 cm². (Or 18 × 12 − 10 × 5 = 166 cm².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 11 × 7 = 77 and 20 × 5 = 100. Add them: 77 + 100 = 177 m². (Or 20 × 12 − 9 × 7 = 177 m².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into three rectangles side by side: 4 × 12 = 48, 8 × (12 − 5) = 8 × 7 = 56, 11 × (12 − 8) = 11 × 4 = 44. Add: 48 + 56 + 44 = 148 cm².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 18 − 8 = 10 m and 9 − 4 = 5 m. Split into two rectangles: 10 × 4 = 40 and 18 × 5 = 90. Area = 40 + 90 = 130 m².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into three rectangles side by side: 4 × 11 = 44, 6 × (11 − 6) = 6 × 5 = 30, 10 × (11 − 8) = 10 × 3 = 30. Add: 44 + 30 + 30 = 104 m².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 14 − 8 = 6 cm and 7 − 4 = 3 cm. Split into two rectangles: 6 × 4 = 24 and 14 × 3 = 42. Area = 24 + 42 = 66 cm².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 20 − 12 = 8 cm and 14 − 5 = 9 cm. Split into two rectangles: 8 × 5 = 40 and 20 × 9 = 180. Area = 40 + 180 = 220 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 5 = 30 and 13 × 4 = 52. Add them: 30 + 52 = 82 cm². (Or 13 × 9 − 7 × 5 = 82 cm².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 5 × 4 = 20 and 11 × 3 = 33. Add them: 20 + 33 = 53 m². (Or 11 × 7 − 6 × 4 = 53 m².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into three rectangles side by side: 6 × 13 = 78, 10 × (13 − 4) = 10 × 9 = 90, 7 × (13 − 7) = 7 × 6 = 42. Add: 78 + 90 + 42 = 210 m².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 9 × 6 = 54 and 20 × 7 = 140. Add them: 54 + 140 = 194 cm². (Or 20 × 13 − 11 × 6 = 194 cm².)

items.q: A rectangle 10 cm by 6 cm has a 2.5 cm by 2 cm rectangle cut from one corner. What area is left?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 10 × 6 = 60 cm². Corner: 2.5 × 2 = 5 cm². 60 − 5 = 55 cm². (55.5 comes from taking away 2.5 + 2 instead of 2.5 × 2.)

items.q: A rectangle is cut out of a larger rectangle. What is the area of the shaded part?
items.e: Big rectangle: 24 × 15 = 360. Hole: 14 × 6 = 84. Shaded part: 360 − 84 = 276 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Take the whole rectangle and subtract the gap: 30 × 16 = 480, gap 14 × 9 = 126. 480 − 126 = 354 cm².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 10 − 6 = 4 m and 8 − 3 = 5 m. Split into two rectangles: 4 × 3 = 12 and 10 × 5 = 50. Area = 12 + 50 = 62 m².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Take the whole rectangle and subtract the gap: 17 × 16 = 272, gap 8 × 10 = 80. 272 − 80 = 192 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Take the whole rectangle and subtract the gap: 26 × 15 = 390, gap 11 × 7 = 77. 390 − 77 = 313 m².

sets.title: Practical problems: tiles, turf, paint and courts

items.q: A netball court is about 30 m long and 15 m wide. About what is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 30 × 15 = 450 m². (30 + 15 + 30 + 15 = 90 m is the distance around it.)

items.q: A rectangular garden bed must have an area of 24 m². One side is 3 m. How much edging goes all the way around it?
items.e: Other side: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 m. Edging: 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 = 22 m.

items.q: This is the plan of an L-shaped backyard. Turf costs $11 per square metre. How much does turf for the whole backyard cost?
items.e: Split into two rectangles: 7 × 3 = 21 and 13 × 5 = 65. Area: 21 + 65 = 86 m². Cost: 86 × $11 = $946.

items.q: A bathroom wall is 2.4 m wide and 2 m high. It is covered with square tiles 20 cm by 20 cm. How many tiles are needed?
items.e: Across: 240 ÷ 20 = 12 tiles. Up: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 tiles. 12 × 10 = 120 tiles.

items.q: A solar panel is 1.7 m long and 1 m wide. A school puts 12 panels on the roof of the hall. What area do the panels cover?
A rug is 3 m by 2 m. A new rug is twice as long and twice as wide. What is the area of the new rug?
items.e: New rug: 6 m by 4 m. Area: 6 × 4 = 24 m². That is 4 times the old area (6 m²), not 2 times.

items.q: A bathroom floor is 3 m long and 2 m wide. It is tiled with square tiles 50 cm by 50 cm. How many tiles are needed?
items.e: Along the length: 300 cm ÷ 50 cm = 6 tiles. Across: 200 cm ÷ 50 cm = 4 tiles. 6 × 4 = 24 tiles. (6 is the area in m², not the number of tiles.)

items.q: A bedroom wall is 4 m long and 3 m high. It has a window 1.5 m by 1 m. What area of wall needs painting?
items.e: Wall: 4 × 3 = 12 m². Window: 1.5 × 1 = 1.5 m². 12 − 1.5 = 10.5 m². (9.5 comes from taking away 1.5 + 1.)

items.q: A wall is 6 m long and 2.5 m high. It needs two coats of paint. One litre of paint covers 10 m². How many litres are needed?
items.e: Wall: 6 × 2.5 = 15 m². Two coats: 2 × 15 = 30 m². 30 ÷ 10 = 3 L. (1.5 L is only one coat.)

items.q: A backyard pool is 10 m long and 4 m wide. The pool cover must be 0.5 m bigger than the pool on every side. What is the area of the cover?
items.e: 0.5 m on each side adds 1 m to each measurement: 11 m by 5 m. Area: 11 × 5 = 55 m². (47.25 comes from adding 0.5 m only once: 10.5 × 4.5.)

items.q: Oliver mows a lawn 12 m long and 8 m wide. He mows about 8 m² each minute. About how long does it take?
items.e: Area: 12 × 8 = 96 m². 96 ÷ 8 = 12 minutes. (5 minutes uses the perimeter, 40 m.)

items.q: A netball court about 30 m long and 15 m wide is marked into three equal thirds along its length. About what is the area of one third?
items.e: Each third is 30 ÷ 3 = 10 m long and 15 m wide: 10 × 15 = 150 m². Check: 3 × 150 = 450 m².

items.q: A patio is 5 m long and 4.5 m wide. Each box of pavers covers 2 m². How many boxes are needed?
items.e: Area: 5 × 4.5 = 22.5 m². 22.5 ÷ 2 = 11.25, so 11 boxes are not enough. Buy 12 boxes.

items.q: A path is 2 m long and 1 m wide. It is paved with bricks 20 cm long and 10 cm wide, long sides along the path. How many bricks are needed?
items.e: Along the path: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 bricks. Across: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 bricks. 10 × 10 = 100 bricks.

items.q: A classroom floor is 9 m long and 7 m wide. New carpet costs $40 per square metre. How much does carpet for the floor cost?
items.e: Area: 9 × 7 = 63 m². Cost: 63 × $40 = $2520. ($1280 uses the perimeter, 32 m.)

items.q: A backyard is 9 m by 5 m. A concrete patio 3 m by 2 m is in one corner. The rest gets turf. How many square metres of turf are needed?
items.e: Backyard: 9 × 5 = 45 m². Patio: 3 × 2 = 6 m². Turf: 45 − 6 = 39 m². (40 comes from taking away 3 + 2.)

items.q: Chloe’s family is laying new turf in a backyard 8 m long and 6.5 m wide. Turf costs $12 per square metre. How much will the turf cost?
items.e: Area: 8 × 6.5 = 52 m². Cost: 52 × $12 = $624. ($348 uses the perimeter, 29 m, instead of the area.)

items.q: A classroom whiteboard is 2.4 m long and 1.2 m high. What is its area?
items.e: 2.4 × 1.2: 24 × 12 = 288, and there are 2 decimal places, so 2.88 m². (3.6 comes from adding.)

items.q: Harper’s bedroom is 4.5 m by 4 m. Grace’s bedroom is 6 m by 3 m. Which bedroom has the larger floor area?
items.e: Harper: 4.5 × 4 = 18 m². Grace: 6 × 3 = 18 m². The areas are the same, even though the perimeters (17 m and 18 m) are different.

items.q: Isla’s class has a vegetable garden bed 4 m long and 2.5 m wide. Each seedling needs 0.5 m². How many seedlings fit in the bed?
items.e: Area: 4 × 2.5 = 10 m². 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 seedlings (there are 2 halves in each square metre).
